items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: to stand on the outside of the fence, there, and listen to Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington, Benny Moten, Cab Calloway, Chick Webb, and just to show you how times have changed, here I am, you are honoring me at a place I couldn’t even come into when

ctx.x: Yeah, him and Coleman Hawkins, that’s in the reed section. Coleman Hawkins, Benny Carter. What a band, I think it was Hilton Jefferson, or Russell Procope, one of the great saxophone players. But Columbus was a great dance town. When you think about those days when you used to go to the dance halls around there. It was the country club there that all the bands used to go play and about three or four years ago, they gave a “Harry Edison Day” there in

Columbus, OH. They gave me the award in the same hall that they wouldn’t let me in, so I made them remember the days when I used to stand on the outside of the fence. They had a wire fence on the outside and all the musicians used to stand on the outside there and listen to all the bands, Ellington and all the big bands, because Columbus was a great dance town. The City Council, they were there, and I told them, “I never thought I’d get to appear in this dance hall because I used to stand on the outside of the…
Must have made it even more satisfying to get an award there.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: He introduced me to Chick Webb.

ctx.x: I thought that was another name but literally it was a craving for that?

Sure, it's your craving for something sweet. And oh, the places, you know -- New York was so great then. It was just a fantastic city. And everybody was so close together. And it was -- oh, they had many of those pads, had the red lights on, and you had all the good records playing for you, like the Billie Holiday records, the Louie Armstrong records. The big bands, Chick Webb, Ella Fitzgerald. Basie would be playing. Don Redman's band would be playing. And he'd just have all those old 78's, you know, just play…
And that was as far as it went, was the pot.
